hints: Use a set or lookup table for membership.
Scan stones once and count each matching character.
Keep uppercase and lowercase letters separate.
title: Jewels and Stones Problem

notes: Each character in stones is counted independently.
The suite covers zero matches, all matches, repetition, case sensitivity, ordering, and maximum-length inputs.
constraints: jewels and stones consist of only English letters.
All the characters of jewels are unique.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]
content.problemStatement:
You're given strings `jewels` representing the types of stones that are jewels, and `stones` representing the stones you have. Each character in `stones` is a type of stone you have. You want to know how many of the stones you have are also jewels.

Letters are case sensitive, so `"a"` is considered a different type of stone from `"A"`.

**Example 1:**

```
Input: jewels = "aA", stones = "aAAbbbb"
Output: 3
```

**Example 2:**

```
Input: jewels = "z", stones = "ZZ"
Output: 0
```

**Constraints:**

* `1 <= jewels.length, stones.length <= 50`
* `jewels` and `stones` consist of only English letters.
* All the characters of `jewels` are **unique**.

notes: Expected output is the JSON-serialised integer returned by numJewelsInStones.
j and s are the lengths of jewels and stones.
solution.approach: Store all jewel characters in a membership set, then scan stones and count every character present in that set.

better.complexity: O(j + s) expected time and O(j) space.
better.description: Use a hash set of jewel characters and make one membership check per stone character.

optimal.complexity: O(j + s) time and O(1) extra space.
optimal.description: Because the alphabet is only 52 English letters, a fixed lookup table can mark jewels and count matches in one pass.

bruteForce.complexity: O(j * s) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
bruteForce.description: For each stone character, scan all jewel characters and count a match.

followUps: Can a fixed 52-entry table replace the hash set?
Why are repeated matching stones counted multiple times?
